lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Sixty-three light-years away, a young star is trailing a tail of dust.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Reported on the eleventh of November, from a study in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The star is called Beta Pictoris. And now Hubble has photographed the tail in ordinary visible light.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: A tail of dust? Around a star?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The tail has a nickname: the Cat's Tail.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The James Webb telescope found it in twenty twenty-four, but only in mid-infrared light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: In visible light it was almost invisible, because the dust is very dark.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: So why could Hubble see it at all?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Patience. Hubble looked at the system six times, between twenty twelve and twenty twenty-five.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Its long exposures pulled out the faint glow of light scattered by the dust.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Together with the Webb data, they suggest the tail lies mostly flat across our view, not pointing toward us.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Earlier estimates said it could stretch up to a thousand astronomical units. About ninety-three billion miles.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The dust is made mostly of carbon-rich material. Each grain is about one micron across.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The grains look porous and fluffy, a bit like tiny sponges, and they soak up most of the light.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Where would so much fluffy dust come from?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One idea: a collision between two bodies the size of Pluto, that made carbon vapor, which cooled into fluffy grains.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The authors say this is uncertain. It fits the evidence, but it needs more observations to confirm.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And this is one young star. It does not show that our own young solar system had the same tail.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: If a figure here is out of date, the sources in the description are the reference.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: So what would you want Hubble and Webb to look at next?
